This goes through the New-Project Entry. Nothing is built: the package is a greeting `main()` and two smoke tests. There is also no spec. `specs/ces-revisions-prompt.md` is your research brief, not a list of numbered requirements, and the three research files are background.

So the outcomes below are candidates drawn from your brief. None is committed until you confirm it.

**A caveat on the cost notes.** I have read your brief in full but only the opening 3,000 characters of each research file. Before writing the roadmap I'll read the data-availability sections (ChatGPT §3.3 and the gap tables), and some estimates may get firmer.

## Outcomes (unranked)

| # | Outcome (what you get) | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|
| O1 | Revision size at each of the four stages, year by year, for national total nonfarm (seasonally adjusted), from real archived vintages | Small data volume (MB). The ALFRED API allows 120 requests/min. How far back usable vintages go is measured by the core stage. |
| O2 | The same, for each NAICS supersector | Roughly 13× O1's series count; still MB. Supersector vintage coverage in ALFRED is unverified. |
| O3 | Unadjusted (NSA) vintages alongside the adjusted ones, so the two can be compared | Doubles the series count. NSA vintage depth is unknown; measured by the core stage. |
| O4 | Whether collection days and first-, second- and third-closing rates change the size of the one-month and two-month revisions | Your time: release dates and the 12th must be hand-built per month from BLS calendars. Closing-rate history depth is unknown until tried. |
| O5 | How much of each adjusted revision comes from re-estimated seasonal factors versus late sample | Needs O3. Model cost is measured by its stage. |
| O6 | Size of the March benchmark error (preliminary and final) by supersector, with wedge-back spread over the months in between | About 40 annual observations per sector, so the estimate will be wide. Benchmark-article tables are hand-collected. |
| O7 | Separate news and noise estimates for each revision stage, from a latent-truth state-space model with covariates in the scale, pooled across supersectors, with 2003 and 2020–22 handled | NUTS runtime: probably hours, but only running it can tell. |
| O8 | Funding, staffing and sample size series, and their association with revision size, reported as descriptive only | Mostly your time: real appropriations, FTE and sample counts hand-built from budget justifications. All three reports say the effect is weakly identified. |

## Proposed tracks

- **A — Vintage data and descriptive revision size (O1–O3): known progression.** Every other track reads this data.
- **B — Collection interval (O4): research.** Split out because its answer stands without the state-space model. A heteroskedastic fit on A's panel answers it, and this sharp within-year variation is the best-identified driver you have.
- **C — Seasonal versus sample decomposition (O5): research.** Its answer stands without B's or D's.
- **D — Benchmark and wedge-back (O6): research.** This is a different stage and a different error source (birth–death, QCEW alignment).
- **E — Joint news/noise model (O7): research.** This is the method that eventually combines B–D. Kept separate so B–D don't wait on its machinery.
- **F — Institutional capacity (O8): research.** Split out because its identification problem is different and its data cost is mostly hand-building.

## Choices already made

- Python 3.14 (`.python-version`) with uv.
- NumPyro/NUTS, Dynamax, Blackjax only if needed, ArviZ and Polars, per your brief. One cheap check before staging: confirm that JAX wheels exist for 3.14.
- National CES all-employee estimates; the estimand is revision scale, not mean bias.

**Proposed name:** `ces-revisions`, giving `specs/ces-revisions-roadmap.md`, which doesn't exist yet.

**Optional probe:** pull the vintage date list for PAYEMS and one supersector from ALFRED (needs your FRED API key). That would turn O1–O3's "unknown depth" into a number. I'll only run it if you say yes.

## One request

Please rank the outcomes within each track and the tracks among themselves, and confirm or change the tracks, their kinds and the name. Also say yes or no to the probe.
